employmentContract.title: Employment Contract Generator
employmentContract.description: Fill in the blanks of Korea's official standard employment contract. Automatic checks for minimum wage, break time and the 52-hour limit, weekly holiday pay, seals and PDF export.

sectionHint.worker: We check the age from the ID number and warn you if the employee is under 18.
sectionHint.guardian: For workers under 18, a parental consent form is generated as the second page. A parent cannot sign the contract on the minor's behalf.
sectionHint.insurance: Industrial accident insurance is mandatory even for one employee. Checked items are marked ■ on the contract.

kindHint.fixed: Fixed-term contract. Using a fixed-term worker for more than 2 years converts them to open-ended employment (Fixed-term Act Art. 4).
kindHint.part: Worker with shorter contractual hours than full-time staff. Working days and hours per day must be stated (Fixed-term Act Art. 17).
kindHint.minor: Standard contract for young workers: max 7 h/day and 35 h/week; family relation certificate and parental consent must be kept on file.

employmentContract.small: Workplace with fewer than 5 regular employees
employmentContract.smallHint: Overtime/night/holiday premiums, annual leave and the 52-hour cap do not apply. Weekly holiday pay, breaks and minimum wage still apply.
employmentContract.fixedTermHint: Check this if the job has an end date, e.g. a vacation job.
employmentContract.perDayHint: For part-time workers, start, end and break times per day should be listed in a table.
employmentContract.breakHint: Leave the break fields empty if there is no break. A 4-hour workday needs at least a 30-minute break, an 8-hour workday at least 1 hour.

summary.payNote: Monthly figures use 365÷7÷12 ≈ 4.345 weeks. Bonuses, allowances and taxes are excluded.

employmentContract.bonusPlaceholder: Twice a year, 50% of base pay
employmentContract.allowanceEmpty: Add meal, transport or position allowances if any.

insight.minWageOk: Hourly {hourly} KRW meets the {year} minimum wage of {min} KRW.
insight.minWageHourly: Minimum wage violation: {hourly} KRW/h is below the {year} minimum of {min} KRW. The shortfall is void and the minimum wage must be paid.
insight.minWageMonthly: Minimum wage violation: monthly pay ÷ {hours} paid hours = {hourly} KRW/h. It must be at least {required} KRW ({short} KRW short).
insight.minWageAllowance: Base pay alone is {hourly} KRW/h, below the {min} KRW minimum. Regular monthly allowances make up the difference, but re-check if some allowances (e.g. overtime pay) don't count toward minimum wage.
insight.holidayPay: {weekly} contractual hours/week → {hours} h of paid weekly holiday, {pay} KRW per week with full attendance. Added to the wage clause.
insight.holidayIncluded: {weekly} contractual hours/week → the monthly pay covers {hours} h including weekly holidays. Stated on the contract.
insight.under15: {weekly} contractual hours/week is under 15, so weekly holiday pay and annual leave do not apply (LSA Art. 18(3)).
insight.breakShort: Insufficient break ({days}): at least 30 min for 4 h and 1 h for 8 h of work, given during working hours (LSA Art. 54).
insight.over52: Over 52 hours: {week} h/week. Only 40 statutory hours plus 12 overtime hours are allowed (LSA Art. 53).
insight.over52Small: {week} h/week. The 52-hour cap does not apply to workplaces under 5 employees, but watch for overwork.
insight.overtime: {hours} h beyond 8 h/day or 40 h/week is overtime. It requires agreement and a 50% premium (about {pay} KRW/month).
insight.overtimeSmall: {hours} h beyond 8 h/day or 40 h/week is overtime. No 50% premium is required under 5 employees, but the hours must be paid (about {pay} KRW/month).
insight.minorOver: Over the limit for minors: up to {day} h/day and {week} h/week. Even with agreement, 8 h/day and 40 h/week cannot be exceeded (LSA Art. 69).
insight.minorConsent: Minors are limited to 7 h/day and 35 h/week. At {day} h/day and {week} h/week, agreement is required (max +1 h/day, +5 h/week).
insight.minorNight: Night work (10 pm–6 am) and holiday work by minors require their consent and MOEL authorization (LSA Art. 70).
insight.holidayOnWorkday: The weekly holiday ({day}) is set on a working day. Choose a day off.
insight.shortInsurance: About {hours} contractual hours/month (under 60). Pension, health and employment insurance generally don't apply, with exceptions (e.g. employment insurance after 3+ months). Industrial accident insurance always applies.
insight.termOrder: The end date is before the start date.
insight.termOver2y: The term exceeds 2 years. A fixed-term worker used for more than 2 years is deemed open-ended (Fixed-term Act Art. 4, with exceptions).
insight.noAccident: Industrial accident insurance is mandatory once you employ anyone, including part-time and short-term workers.
insight.ageMinor: The employee is {age}. If under 18, choose the 'Under 18' type to add parental consent and hour limits.
insight.ageAdult: The employee is {age}, i.e. 18 or older. A regular type can be used.
insight.under15Age: The employee is {age}. Children under 15 need an employment permit from MOEL (LSA Art. 64).
insight.minorDocs: When employing a minor, keep a family relation certificate and parental consent at the workplace (LSA Art. 66). The consent form is generated as page 2.
insight.smallNote: Under 5 employees: annual leave is marked as not applicable. The duty to issue a written contract and its penalties still apply.

guide.title: Employment contract essentials
guide.intro: Every Korean employer — including those hiring part-timers, trainees or short-term staff (except businesses employing only cohabiting relatives) — must issue a written employment contract to the employee. This generator follows the Ministry of Employment and Labor's standard form and flags minimum wage, break and working-hour violations as you type.

sections.title: Required terms (LSA Art. 17)
items: Wages: components, calculation and payment method
Wages, hours, holidays and leave must be given in writing; electronic documents are allowed.

sections.title: Penalties
items: Failure to state and issue terms in writing: fine up to 5 million KRW (LSA Art. 114)
For fixed-term/part-time workers, an administrative fine up to 5 million KRW per worker may also apply (Fixed-term Act Art. 24)
If wages or hours change, the new terms must be issued in writing again
Issue a copy even if not requested, and keep a signed receipt

sections.title: Part-time workers
items: Working days and hours per day must be stated (Fixed-term Act Art. 17)
15+ hours/week earns weekly holiday pay and annual leave; under 15 earns neither
Work beyond contractual hours needs consent, max 12 h/week, 50% premium (5+ employees)
2026 minimum wage 10,320 KRW/h; 2,156,880 KRW/month for 40 h/week (209 h)

sections.title: Workers under 18
items: Max 7 h/day and 35 h/week, +1 h/day and +5 h/week by agreement (LSA Art. 69)
Keep a family relation certificate and parental consent on file (Art. 66)
Parents cannot sign on the minor's behalf; the minor claims wages directly (Arts. 67–68)
Night (10 pm–6 am) and holiday work require consent and MOEL authorization (Art. 70)

items.q: Do part-time jobs need a written contract?
items.a: Yes. One-day jobs, trainees and all employees must receive a written contract. Not issuing wages, hours, holidays and leave in writing can lead to a fine up to 5 million KRW (LSA Art. 114), and part-time workers can also trigger an administrative fine up to 5 million KRW under the Fixed-term Act.

items.q: When must the contract be signed?
items.a: When the employment begins, before work starts, with a copy handed to the employee right away. If wages or hours change, issue the new terms in writing again.

items.q: How do I check minimum wage for monthly pay?
items.a: Divide base pay plus regular monthly allowances by monthly contractual hours plus weekly holiday hours. For 40 h/week that is 209 hours, so the 2026 monthly minimum is 10,320 × 209 = 2,156,880 KRW. This tool calculates it from the hours you enter.

items.q: Should weekly holiday pay be written in the contract?
items.a: With 15+ contractual hours a week and full attendance, a paid weekly holiday arises. For hourly pay it is often paid separately, so stating the amount prevents disputes; for monthly pay it is usually stated as included. This tool fills it in automatically.

items.q: Do workplaces with fewer than 5 employees need contracts?
items.a: Yes. The written contract duty, minimum wage, weekly holidays and breaks apply. Overtime/night/holiday premiums, annual leave and the 52-hour cap do not.

items.q: What documents are needed to hire a student under 18?
items.a: The young worker standard contract, a family relation certificate and parental consent. Hours are limited to 7 h/day and 35 h/week, and under-15s need an employment permit. Choosing 'Under 18' generates the consent form as page 2.
